currentContext.expansion: The Company's expansion centres on a single greenfield project: a second cashew processing facility at Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh, on a site of 7,73,190 sq ft. Land was acquired during FY 2025-26, construction is advancing and machinery has been specified and is being sourced. The facility is stated to add 35,000 MT of processing capacity, taking the total from 18,000 MT towards 53,000 MT, and to bring geographic diversification and operational resilience alongside the existing Anakapalli plant. It is funded principally from the December 2025 BSE SME listing, which raised Rs 74.45 crores, of which Rs 57 crores is being deployed into land development, civil construction and the installation of advanced machinery; by the close of FY 2025-26 purchase orders worth Rs 39.53 crores had been issued against this plan with Rs 10.47 crores advanced. A further Rs 10.43 crores was earmarked for general corporate purposes, focused on the Royal Mewa brand, working capital and business development. The plant will carry advanced shelling, modern colour-sorting and precision quality-control equipment intended to lift yield and consistency, and will incorporate the effluent, sewage treatment, water-softening and reverse-osmosis infrastructure used at the existing facility, together with a creche, canteen and occupational health centre. The existing Anakapalli facility was itself expanded to 18,000 MTPA during FY 2025-26, from an initial 7,000 MTPA on acquisition in 2021, and ran at close to 86% utilisation through the year. No commissioning or ramp date for Vizianagaram is disclosed anywhere in the routed text. Export ambition is tied to the project: the Company aims to establish a presence across nine international markets across the Middle East, Asia, Europe and Southeast Asia following its commissioning.
